title: Hard-wall transverse-vector spectrum
summary: A shooting and collocation reproduction of the transverse-vector spectrum on the standard hard-wall AdS/QCD slice.

source.title: QCD and a Holographic Model of Hadrons

conventions.name: radial interval
conventions.value: epsilon <= z <= z_m on a fixed AdS_5 slice
conventions.rationale: The IR wall is a phenomenological cutoff rather than a dynamically derived geometry.

conventions.name: UV boundary condition
conventions.rationale: Finite-cutoff Dirichlet approximation to the normalizable vector mode.

conventions.name: IR boundary condition
conventions.rationale: Standard Neumann condition used by the source model.

conventions.name: comparison normalization
conventions.rationale: The ratios remove the single hard-wall scale z_m.

parameters.name: hard-wall position
parameters.description: Positive IR-wall position; the benchmark default is not a phenomenological fit.

equations.description: Normal-mode equation for a transverse flavor-vector field on the AdS_5 slice.
Zero-cutoff eigenvalues are positive zeros of the Bessel function J_0.

observables.name: ground-state-normalized vector-mode masses
observables.extraction: Ordered finite-cutoff eigenvalues divided by the lowest eigenvalue.

acceptance_criteria: The first four shooting mass ratios agree with the analytic Bessel-zero ratios within 5e-4.
Adaptive shooting and global collocation agree on their first four ratios within 1e-3.
Three decreasing UV cutoffs monotonically reduce the maximum analytic-ratio error.

tests.expected: The numerical ratios reproduce the first four J_0-zero ratios within tolerance.
Shooting and collocation agree within the declared cross-solver tolerance.
The maximum ratio error decreases across all three cutoff levels.

claims.statement: The standard hard-wall vector spectrum approaches the positive J_0 zeros when the UV cutoff vanishes.
claims.evidence: Erlich et al., arXiv:hep-ph/0501128v2, Eq. (5) and the vector-mode discussion.

claims.statement: The HoloForge shooting and collocation routes reproduce the first four normalized Bessel-zero masses within their declared tolerances.
claims.evidence: Automated analytic, cross-solver, and cutoff-refinement tests in tests/test_hard_wall_vector.py.

limitations: The IR wall and its boundary condition are phenomenological inputs rather than consequences derived from QCD.
The finite UV cutoff creates a separate approximation error even when the numerical solver converges.
The benchmark does not test decay constants, chiral observables, or the global phenomenological adequacy of the hard-wall model.
